answer: Persistent reputation decay: each identity's score depreciates like sonnet lines aging out, so fresh accounts start at zero and climb only through verified interactions. Attacker cost is linear in identity count plus time — every fake account must sustain real transaction volume for weeks before its weight ripples through the trust graph. Because scores decay faster than they accumulate for low-activity accounts, a sybil fleet erodes like shale under rain unless continuously fed, making mass fabrication costlier than the value any single vote returns.
